recommended_price_summary: Proposed prices, INR, before 18% GST, valid until 3 Nov 2026. Lead with A, the 2-week pilot for 50 builders at Rs 75,000 fixed (Rs 88,500 with GST; arithmetic 50 x Rs 1,500; highlighted as the recommended option). B is the monthly managed run for 150 builders at Rs 45,000 a month (Rs 53,100 with GST), offered only after the pilot and cancellable at any month end, plus an optional shared-risk version of Rs 30,000 + Rs 3,000 per demo held. C is a research-only list at Rs 18,500 for 50 builders or Rs 35,000 for 150. WhatsApp fees are passed through at cost: about Rs 30 to 310 for the pilot (cap Rs 500) and Rs 90 to 930 a month (cap Rs 1,500). One mid-level sales employee costs about Rs 36,900 a month all-in, so the monthly run is about 1.2 times one employee and is not cheaper on cost alone. The proposal says this openly. The pilot costs about 2 months of one employee. Payment terms are suggested as 50% on approval and 50% at the Day 14 report. All numbers sit in prices.json.
whatsapp_message_text:
Hi Sridhar, thank you for the call today. The proposal is attached as a PDF: how the research and WhatsApp outreach work, a sample dashboard and page, a two-week pilot with pass and fail rules agreed in advance, the estimate, and the comparison with hiring a sales executive. All prices are proposals and can change after your feedback. When would a 15-minute screen-share of the dashboard, page and video suit you this week?

IV Infotech
decisions_for_owner: Confirm the lead price and structure. The monthly run (Rs 45,000) costs more than one employee (Rs 36,900 all-in) and the proposal says so. Keep it, lower it, or keep the shared-risk alternative (switch show_alternative in prices.json).

Pilot pass/fail rules: I relaxed the cost workstream's strict 'at least 2 genuine replies' gate, because 50 builders will probably deliver fewer than 30 owner-level messages. Measure 3 is now 'pass or inconclusive'. Keep my version or restore the strict gate (table_gates() in build_proposal.py and the Decision rule paragraph in proposal_template.html).

Whether Sridhar sees real owner names on page 3 (show_owner_names in prices.json; individuals and unknowns are anonymised either way) and whether to disclose '9 contacted, no replies' (show_campaign1_reply_count; 2 of 7 on time stays).

Whether to keep the correction on page 9 telling him to disregard the first pitch's '92+ staff hours' and 'Rs 23,000+ monthly overhead saved', and the offer to ask MP RERA for permission (not promised).

First-touch channel and sender: the proposal promises WhatsApp templates from IV Infotech's line to business-published numbers (10 to 25 a day, STOP line, stop on any Meta warning) with a separate +91 number recommended. Alternative is a first touch from Sridhar's own number or an office-line call. I wrote 'IV Infotech's line' and not 'verified', because business verification status is unknown.
Build the forward-only reply rule for this account before any send: today a first inbound reply reaches the AI sales agent first, and the proposal promises no bot ever answers a builder-owner.

Do not send dashboard/dashboard.html as it is: its builder table shows real names with invented statuses that contradict the enrichment test (e.g. Shri Balajee marked Likely, our test found Unknown; Dee Vee marked Message approved). The PDF uses only the pipeline strip and the example lead with invented names. Skip that table on any screen share or get a version with every real row set to Researched / Unknown.

Payment terms (50/50 suggested), validity (14 days), whether to credit part of the pilot against month 1 (not in the document), data export and exit terms (not yet written), and Sridhar's title ('Founder' vs solo developer / acting CTO).
open_gaps: Our BSP (Fortius) per-message rate, plan fee, markup and INR billing status are unknown. The pass-through estimate assumes Rs 1.02 to Rs 1.29 per message and no markup; Meta's INR rate (Rs 0.8631) comes from a news report, not Meta's own rate card.
Our Meta quality rating and business verification status are unknown; a Meta restriction on our shared line is an unpriced risk.

Hours and margin behind the price conflict between workstreams: Rs 1,000/hour with 30% margin (price built on this) versus Rs 375/hour (cost to serve about Rs 13,600 to 21,400 a month). There may be room to lower the monthly fee.

Real-owner hit rate rests on n = 6 (owner named 4 of 6, direct owner WhatsApp number 0 of 6). The 5 to 20 owner-level messages for the pilot and the employee cost components, hiring time and research hours are assumptions, and Sridhar's own contract value, demo volume and hiring cost are unknown.

Hindi lines on the page and video have no native-speaker check, Sridhar's screen recordings, logo, voice and permissions are not in hand (the video is a storyboard, not a rendered MP4), and every product line comes from nexus360.in and needs his confirmation.
Dashboard funnel middle counts (146/135/131) differ slightly from the dashboard workstream's own replay (151/140/136); the proposal uses the saved script summary. Start (2,173) and end (72) match.

Pilot is too small to give a reply-rate verdict; about 150 builders (the first month of the run) is needed. Hand-off alert timing and the 'stop after a reply' rule are not yet measured or built for this account.
Cost workstream's 5-minute video render figure conflicts with the measured 40 seconds; no render time is in the proposal, so the price is unaffected.
